raw: this is a long one so bear with me i want to record everything that went through my head about the platform migration because i know i will forget half of it by tomorrow first the history we started with a single server in the office and everything ran on it the database the web app the batch jobs and even the file share it worked for years until the day the disk filled up and the whole thing stopped for six hours that was the day we decided to move to the cloud then we spent three months arguing about which provider to use and in the end we picked the one where anirudh menon already had an account which is not a great reason but it was good enough second the architecture the new setup has a kubernetes cluster with three nodes a managed postgres database and an object store for the uploads terraform describes all of it so in theory we can rebuild everything from scratch in under an hour in practice we have never tried third the problems the biggest one was the database connection limit the old server never cared how many connections you opened but the managed one cuts you off at a hundred so every service needed a pooler and nobody told the batch jobs which opened a connection for every row the second problem was the time zone the old server was in india standard time and the new one is in utc so for two days every report showed the wrong date and we only noticed because sofia kowalczyk asked why her screenshot from monday said tuesday fourth the lessons we should have moved one service at a time we should have written the rollback plan before the move not during it and we should have asked the people who use the reports what they actually need instead of guessing fifth what is next we still have two services on the old server the invoice generator and the email sender the plan is to move the email sender first because it is stateless and then the invoice generator after we fix its file path assumptions after that we switch off the old server and finally get to delete the file share which i have been waiting to do for three years and one last thing before i forget the monitoring needs the same treatment as the services so we should write the alerts as code too and review them like any other change because the alerts we have today were all created by hand during incidents and nobody remembers why half of them exist
